newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BERGKAMP LIFTS ARSENAL TO 3-1 WIN OVER EVERTON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BERGKAMP LIFTS ARSENAL TO 3-1 WIN OVER EVERTON.

text.p: Dennis Bergkamp at his majestic best inspired Arsenal to a 3-1 win over Everton on Sunday as the north London side stepped up their challenge for the premier league title.

Bergkamp, who now begins a three-match suspension after being sent off against Sunderland, opened the scoring 10 minutes after the interval and two minutes later Frenchman Patrick Vieira put the home side further ahead.

Paul Merson scored Arsenal's third goal after Bergkamp stole the ball off Dave Watson at the halfway line. The Dutchman strode through the Everton defence and unleashed a thunderous shot which Neville Southall parried to Merson who tapped the ball in to an empty net.
Duncan Ferguson grabbed a goal in the last minute for Everton when he rose high above the Arsenal defenders and headed the ball past David Seaman.
Arsenal now have 43 points, three behind leaders Liverpool and one adrift of second-placed Manchester United.

Striker Ian Wright, returning after a three-month suspension, played the first half only before he was taken off as a precaution after sustaining a hamstring strain. Midfielder David Platt also injured a hamstring and is likely to miss England's World Cup qualifier against Italy on February 12.
Brian Roy scored twice for Nottingham Forest in their 2-1 win over Arsenal's north London rivals Tottenham Hotspur after Andy Sinton had opened the scoring for Spurs in the 75th second.
Tottenham looked to be in control in the first half before Swiss Ramon Vega was sent off just before the interval for lashing out at Forest's Colin Cooper.
Manager Gerry Francis, whose side have now lost their last four games in a row, was incensed with Vega who was playing in just his second match for Tottenham.
"I don't want players sent off for silly incidents," he said. "They've got to keep their discipline. It's the first time I've had a player sent off since I've been here."
The first division produced one of the greatest comebacks in soccer history when Queen's Park Ranger recovered from 4-0 after 21 minutes to draw 4-4 with Port Vale.
The visitors scored three goals in the final five minutes with John Spencer grabbing the equaliser in injury time.
